messages:
josh (customer): Hey all — hit a weird 401 on our Dedicated/private deployment. Calls to /v1/generate are returning 401 from the runtime; we confirmed the client sends Authorization: Bearer <token> but the backend logs show no Authorization header. Happening only when traffic passes through customer's LB + Istio ingressgateway (VPC). Can someone help triage?

irene (support): Sorry you're blocked — can you paste a minimal repro (curl -v) and the runtime access logs showing the missing header? Also which gateway (Istio version, nginx, cloud LB)?

josh (customer): Sure. Istio 1.18, AWS NLB in front, then istio-ingressgateway. Repro curl I ran from an external machine: 
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer TESTTOK123" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  https://api.example.internal/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```
curl -v shows Authorization header in request. But runtime log line (pod logs for model-runtime) shows: 
```
[2025-10-12T14:02:13Z] "POST /v1/generate" 401 - headers: {"host":"api.example.internal","content-type":"application/json","x-forwarded-for":"3.4.5.6"}
```
No Authorization.

devon (eng-platform): OK likely suspects: (1) Envoy ext_authz (external auth) or oauth2-proxy is stripping/consuming the header, (2) LB doing TLS termination + not forwarding proxied header, (3) an Istio EnvoyFilter or Gateway VirtualService header rewrite. Quick checks: 
- Verify envoy filters: `istioctl proxy-config listeners <ingress-pod> -n istio-system` and `istioctl proxy-config route <ingress-pod> -n istio-system` to look for header_manipulation sections.
- Check for ext_authz config: `istioctl proxy-config listeners <pod> | grep ext_authz -n` or dump config: `kubectl exec -n istio-system <ingress-pod> -- curl -sS localhost:15000/config_dump | jq '.configs[] | select(.type=="http")'`

anya (eng-runtime): Another common one: oauth2-proxy (or similar) will validate and then drop Authorization unless configured to pass it upstream. If customer has a sidecar or ext-auth service, they often replace it with their own header (e.g., X-Forwarded-User) and remove the token. Ask: Do you have an auth service in front of ingress?

josh (customer): Yes, they run an external auth service in front of the gateway (company SSO). I think it's oauth2-proxy. How do I confirm it's the one removing the header?

irene (support): Two quick ways: (A) curl directly to the ingressgateway pod (port-forward) to bypass the NLB and see if header still disappears; (B) curl from ingressgateway to runtime to see what headers it sends upstream. Commands: 
```
# port-forward to ingressgateway (local)
kubectl -n istio-system port-forward svc/istio-ingressgateway 15080:80 150443:443
# from your laptop (direct to ingressgateway)
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer TESTTOK123" https://127.0.0.1:150443/v1/generate --insecure

# exec into ingress pod and curl upstream runtime service (simulate path)
kubectl -n istio-system exec -it <ingress-pod> -- /bin/sh -c "curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer TESTTOK123' http://<runtime-svc>.<ns>.svc.cluster.local:8080/v1/generate"
```
If the exec shows Authorization present gone at runtime, the ingress is stripping.

devon (eng-platform): If it's oauth2-proxy: check arg `--pass-authorization-header` (oauth2-proxy) or similar flag. If using ext_authz filter, check whether the authz server responds with `headers_to_add` or `remove` instructions. In Envoy ext_authz, the authz server can instruct to remove headers.

anya (eng-runtime): I had this exact issue on another customer: oauth2-proxy validated the cookie, then forwarded a new Authorization header as `Bearer <internal_token>` but only when `--pass-access-token` was set. Otherwise it removed the header. Also note nginx controllers require `proxy_set_header Authorization $http_authorization;` in the config. For Istio you can patch the Gateway to preserve headers: in a VirtualService/Gateway you can use `headers: request: set: {}` or add an EnvoyFilter that ensures `authorization` is not in the `remove_request_headers` list.

josh (customer): Ran the port-forward test — same result, header missing at runtime. I also found oauth2-proxy deployment. Its args don't include --pass-authorization-header. We don't want to relay raw user tokens upstream for security, but Redwood API needs the token (we use token scopes). Is there a recommended pattern?

irene (support): Two approaches: 
1) If you want the original token to reach the runtime: configure oauth2-proxy / ext-auth to forward the header (set `--pass-authorization-header=true` or equivalent). Ensure the auth component isn't normalizing or replacing header name casing (Authorization must be exact).
2) If you prefer auth service to mint a short-lived internal token for the runtime: have the auth service add a header like `X-Forwarded-Authorization: Bearer <internal>` and then configure an EnvoyFilter on the ingress to map that header back to `Authorization` before proxying upstream. Example EnvoyFilter snippet: 
```yaml
apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1alpha3
kind: EnvoyFilter
metadata:
  name: map-xfwd-auth-to-authorization
  namespace: istio-system
spec:
  workloadSelector:
    labels:
      app: istio-ingressgateway
  configPatches:
  - applyTo: NETWORK_FILTER
    match:
      context: GATEWAY
    patch:
      operation: MERGE
      value:
        name: envoy.filters.http.router
        typed_config:
          '@type': type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.http.router.v3.Router
          start_child_span: true
  - applyTo: HTTP_FILTER
    match:
      context: GATEWAY
      listener:
        filterChain:
          filter:
            name: envoy.filters.network.http_connection_manager
    patch:
      operation: INSERT_BEFORE
      value:
        name: envoy.filters.http.header_to_metadata
        typed_config:
          '@type': type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.http.header_to_metadata.v3.Config
          request_rules:
          - header: "x-forwarded-authorization"
            remove: true
            on_header_present:
              metadata_namespace: envoy.lb
              key: forwarded_auth
```
(above is illustrative — we'll need to craft a small Lua or header-rewrite filter to set Authorization header).

devon (eng-platform): If you don't want to manage EnvoyFilter YAML, simpler: change oauth2-proxy to set header `X-Forwarded-Authorization` and then add this tiny Lua filter on ingress to copy X-Forwarded-Authorization -> Authorization: 
```yaml
filters:
- name: envoy.filters.http.lua
  typed_config:
    '@type': type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.http.lua.v3.Lua
    inline_code: |
      function envoy_on_request(request_handle)
        local h = request_handle:headers():get("x-forwarded-authorization")
        if h then
          request_handle:headers():add("authorization", h)
        end
      end
```
This avoids sending the original token to the internet but provides a short-lived internal token to the runtime.

josh (customer): Good options. For now we enabled `--pass-authorization-header=true` in oauth2-proxy and redeployed; request to runtime now shows Authorization header present and 200. Thanks.

anya (eng-runtime): Great. Follow-ups: 
- If you leave `pass-authorization-header`, audit logs and token scopes — ensure tokens are audience-limited to runtime.
- If using internal tokens, use signed short-lived JWTs and validate them in runtime.
- We should add a KB entry for Dedicated/Private deployments documenting common causes (oauth2-proxy, ext_authz, LB config, nginx proxy_set_header) and sample EnvoyFilter and Lua snippet.

irene (support): Filing a short KB and linking it in the support runbook. Also marking this thread resolved. :white_check_mark:

sre-bot: incident-note:ticket-8901 updated by irene — resolution: enabled pass-auth header on oauth2-proxy (customer side).

josh (customer): Thanks everyone — saved my Friday. :tada:
